title: Stop pasting tool output into the prompt
caption:
Your AI agent is drowning in its own tool output. A new Tsinghua paper compresses tool results into latent tokens instead of text: 70 to 89 percent fewer tokens, up to 56 percent faster, and more accurate.

Paper: arxiv.org/abs/2611.06500
Code: github.com/THU-Agent/Coca-cola

scenes.narration: Every tool call your agent makes pastes thousands of tokens of noise into its memory. A new paper says: stop.
scenes.title: Stop pasting tool output into the prompt.

scenes.narration: The usual loop: call a tool, dump the raw output into context, and make the model read all of it before the next action.
scenes.title: The usual agent loop

scenes.narration: Long, noisy observations eat the context window and dilute attention. Summaries help, but text can only be squeezed so far.
scenes.title: Why text is the bottleneck
lines: Raw outputs are long and noisy
They crowd out the actual task
Text summaries hit a compression floor

scenes.narration: The fix, called Coca-Cola, compresses each tool output into a few latent tokens: vectors in the model's embedding space instead of words.
scenes.title: Compress to latent tokens

scenes.narration: It is trained so the agent's next action stays the same with the full output or the compressed one. Action-preserving training.
scenes.title: Train for the same next action
lines: Same next action, full or compressed

scenes.narration: Across four QA benchmarks, token use fell 70 to 89 percent, runtime 24 to 56 percent, and accuracy went up.
scenes.title: Fewer tokens, faster, better

scenes.narration: Tools don't need to speak in text. Paper and code from Tsinghua, links in the caption.
scenes.title: Tools don't need to speak in text.
scenes.cta: Follow for one AI paper a day
